family_78b.engine_rule: PP4 (the lead's ruling, 5 Nov 2026): every wrapper kind runs on engine X (engine_x above): untuned_answers, rep_pass, l1_scan and classifier on the pod; l1_score, s3_score, score_edit, add_edit and s_pool on the Mac. Every derived settings file carries engine_x unchanged from the 1B file, and the frozen check_settings refuses another engine identity (R: scripts/stage1/s1common.py:589-591). A run on engine Y needs the settings re-derived for Y (engine_x = Y's identity, a new PINS-78B.json, a new PINS_FILE_SHA256) by a recorded step; none exists. The engine's own jobs (the a0-1101 retrain, a1_pass) follow ruling 10 and addendum A13, not this rule. The kit packs scorer pods with engine X.
family_78b.rule: the 1B file's schema and name, so scripts/stage1's unchanged check_settings accepts it; every value that differs from the 1B file is per family (pins_78b.json) or a documented 7-8B rule; a null is a pin that waits for the event named in waits; scorers_78b.py refuses a command while a pin it needs is null

inputs: REQ-3's rows file and summary (the pools s3_safe and s3_orig listed with the SHA-256s that REQ-6's and REQ-9's records name); REQ-6's s_pool_record.json; REQ-9's untuned_answers_record.json; each by SHA-256
name: score_s3_datarx
next: write_score_add.py (scorer s3) selects the top 48; write_add_edit.py (list s3) writes the add edit
reports: S1's SAS; |S1 & S3 subset|; the share of the subset's y^orig that the lexicon calls REFUSAL-OPENING; the capped count; the ids leaving the ranking by encode_train's reason; per-layer s^l of both responses, so the scores can be recomputed
requirement: REQ-11 (brief rev 1; RS B8; SPEC sections 3.4-3.6); lead decisions L10, L14 (1); the lead's Part C requirement (model-agnostic); 7-8B: Part 1 section 14 item 1 (S3 from the family's own untuned answers; CHECK C6); Mac, $0
rule: h^l = read (a) at hidden-state indices l = 1..n (the embedding output excluded; index n = model.norm of the last block's output, L4); s^l(d) = cos(h^l, C_r^l) - cos(h^l, C_c^l) with C_r = the 64 safe anchors' mean and C_c = the 64 harmful anchors' mean (REQ-3's cos_safe - cos_harmful); R(d) = the mean over l; SAS(x) = R(x, y^safe) - R(x, y^orig); only the S3 subset (1,000) is ranked; a y^orig that encode_train refused leaves the ranking and is counted (L14 (1)); S1's 48 rows get their SAS reported (L10 (2))
